info.title: Ottie API
info.description: The HTTP API of the Ottie daemon (`ottie serve`): every client (web UI, desktop and Android apps, browser extension, scripts) goes through it. How to use it, with examples: docs/api/README.md in the repository.

servers.description: A daemon on this computer, at the default address

get.summary: Who this token is, and which folders devices may use.

200.description: This token's device (null: the computer running Ottie) and the folders devices may use

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

get.summary: Every device with a token of its own. Only for the computer running Ottie.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `ownerOnly`

post.summary:
Gives a device a token of its own, full or read-only. The token is in
this answer only: Ottie keeps a hash of it. Only for the computer running

400.description: `invalidDeviceName`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `ownerOnly`

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

Takes a device's token away: its requests are refused from now on, and

Replaces the folders chosen in Settings, besides those of config.toml.

400.description: `relativeFolder`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `ownerOnly`

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

400.description: `invalidCategoryName`, `invalidExtension`, `relativeFolder`, `nonUtf8Path` or `outOfRange` (`speedLimit`)

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`, or `folderNotAllowed`: a device's folder outside the folders it may use

The category a link would get if added without one (in that folder, if

in an address or a log.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

Replaces every setting of a category. A new folder applies to downloads

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

delete.summary:
Removes a category. Its downloads move to General first (a `changed`
event for each); their files stay where they are.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

get.summary: Every certificate trusted by hand, oldest first.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

post.summary:
Trusts a server's certificate from now on. Trusting one already trusted
answers with it.

400.description: `invalidCertificate`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

400.description: `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

get.summary:
Live changes, as a WebSocket of JSON `Event` messages. Offer the
protocols `ottie.v1` and `ottie.token.<token>` (browsers can't set headers
here); the server picks `ottie.v1`. Connect first, then fetch the lists
(`GET /jobs`, …), then apply events in order; on `resync`, fetch again.

101.description: The WebSocket is open; each message is an `Event`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no `ottie.token.<token>` protocol with the right token

post.summary:
Proves the daemon knows this computer's token, without the token: the
answer is HMAC-SHA256(token, "ottie identity v1\n" + nonce), as hex.
Needs no token; ask it before sending one.

400.description: `invalidBody`: the nonce isn't 32 to 128 hex digits

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

post.summary:
Queues a download. It starts as soon as a slot is free, or waits for
its start time (`scheduled`) if it has one. Sent again with the same
`requestId`, it answers the first one's ID instead of adding another.

400.description: `invalidUrl`, `unsupportedScheme`, `relativeFolder`, `nonUtf8Path`, `noFolder`, `stopBeforeStart`, `outOfRange` (`startAt`, `stopAt`: past the end of year 9999) or `invalidRequestId`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`, or `folderNotAllowed`: a device's `destDir` outside the folders it may use

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
Queues several downloads at once, in order, each as `POST /jobs` would.
Those that can be added are, even if others are refused: the answer
gives each one's ID or why it was refused. Clients hear of each one added
through a `changed` event (many at once may come as a `resync`).

200.description: Each one's ID, or why it was refused

400.description: `tooManyLinks`: more than the setting `maxBatch`; none added

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
The links in some text (one per line, an email, a web page): in order,
each once, with what adding each would do. Anything of the form
`scheme://…` counts, so links that can't be added are listed too, with
why. Nothing is added. A POST, so links, which may carry tokens, never
sit in an address or a log. A device's `destDir` must be one it may
write to: whether a file is there is never looked up anywhere else.

400.description: `tooManyLinks` (more than the setting `maxBatch`) or `relativeFolder`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `folderNotAllowed`: a device's `destDir` outside its folders

post.summary:
Moves downloads in the queue, among the waiting (queued, scheduled or paused)
downloads of their priority: priority comes first, the place only orders
downloads of the same one. Those moved keep their order among themselves,
so neighbours move as a block. Downloads that aren't waiting stay as they
are; next to a download (`before`, `after`), so do those of another
priority than it. Every client hears of each one that moved through a
`changed` event (its new `place`).

400.description: `invalidJobId`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

delete.summary:
Takes a download off the list, in any state. Stops it first if it's
running (answering once it has) and deletes its partial file; a completed
file stays on disk.

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

patch.summary:
Changes a download's own speed limit, priority, streaming mode, start
and stop time (the fields given), in any state; they take effect at
once, even while it runs. A start time to come makes it `scheduled` (a
running download stops first, and its `changed` event comes once it
has). Every client hears of it through one `changed` event, none if
nothing changed.

400.description: `invalidJobId`, `stopBeforeStart` or `outOfRange` (`speedLimit`, `startAt`, `stopAt`); or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

409.description: Times for a finished download (`invalidTransition`), or `jobMoving`

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
Stops a download for good and deletes its partial file. It stays on the
list as `cancelled`.

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
Moves a download to another category, as the user's choice (never
re-matched), and its file to that category's folder. A running download
stops, moves and carries on. Answers once the file has moved, which
between drives takes as long as a copy. A category without a folder
leaves the file where it is.

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `moveFailed`: the file couldn't move (disk full…)

post.summary: Pauses a download. Answers once it has really stopped and its file is flushed.

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
Puts a paused or failed download back in the queue; a scheduled one
joins it now, without waiting for its start time.

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
A download's play link, as a path on this server: the same one while it
is in use. It ends with the file name once known, so players can show it.

400.description: `invalidJobId`; or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

200.description: The OpenAPI description of this API

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one
`unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

patch.summary:
Changes the settings given, all at once; each is saved and takes effect
at once. Every client hears of it through a `settingsChanged` event. One
value out of range refuses the whole change.

400.description: `outOfRange` (with the setting and its range) or `invalidLanguage`

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

get.summary: Every time slot, in the order of the list, and the time zone they follow.

200.description: Every slot, and the time zone

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

post.summary:
Adds a slot at the end of the list (the lowest: others win over it). It
applies at once if it covers now.

400.description: `slotWithoutDays`, `slotWithoutEffect`, `invalidTime` or `outOfRange` (`maxConcurrent`, `speedLimit`)

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

post.summary:
Puts the slots in a new order (the higher one wins where two apply to

`slotChanged` event.

400.description: `invalidSlotOrder`: not every slot once

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

put.summary: Replaces a slot; it applies at once.

400.description: `slotWithoutDays`, `slotWithoutEffect`, `invalidTime` or `outOfRange` (`maxConcurrent`, `speedLimit`); or `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

delete.summary: Removes a slot; what it held or limited goes back to normal.

400.description: `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

403.description: `readOnly`: a device's token that may only read

500.description: `storageFailed`: the change couldn't be saved, so nothing changed

get.summary:
The total download speed, one sample per second, oldest first: up to the
last hour, since the daemon started. Each running download's speed is
estimated from its progress (smoothed), then they're added up. A client
keeps it going from the `progress` events.

200.description: Up to an hour of samples

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

get.summary: The same as `GET /stream/{ticket}/{name}`, without the name.

400.description: `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

get.summary:
Plays a download, complete or not: no token, the ticket in the path is
the permission. Bytes that haven't arrived yet are waited for (also while
the download is queued or paused). The answer breaks off if the download
fails, is cancelled or removed, or starts over. `Range` works when the
size is known (`Accept-Ranges: bytes`).

parameters.description: The file name; only for players to show

200.description: The whole file, as it arrives

400.description: `invalidPath`: a parameter in the path can't be read

409.description: `downloadStopped`: it failed or was cancelled before it had a file

416.description: The range starts past the end (`Content-Range: bytes */<size>`)

401.description: `unauthorized`: no token, or the wrong one

AccessInfo.description:
Who a token belongs to, and the folders devices may use: `GET /access`
(docs/decisions/0052).

oneOf.description:
The device this token was given to; null for the computer running
Ottie (its token file's token), which alone manages devices and folders.

readOnly.description: It may look but not change anything.

category.description: Default: matched by the file's extension.

cookie.description:
For a download a browser hands over (the extension): its `Cookie`
header for this link, sent again with every request of this download
and no other. Kept by the daemon, never given back.

destDir.description: An absolute folder. Default: the category's folder.

oneOf.description:
What to do if a file with its name is already in its folder, when the
server answers. Default: the settings' `existing`.

referrer.description: The page it came from (`Referer`), the same way.

requestId.description:
Makes sending it again safe (docs/decisions/0060): a client that got
no answer (a timeout, a lost connection) sends the same body with the
same `requestId`, and gets the first one's answer instead of a second
download, for 10 minutes (until Ottie restarts). Per token; 1 to 64
letters, digits, `-` or `_`, random (a UUID). Ignored in
`POST /jobs/batch`.

startAt.description:
Wait until then (`scheduled`), in milliseconds since 1970 (UTC).
Default, or a time already past: queued at once.

stopAt.description: Pause then if it hasn't finished, the same way. After `startAt`.

streaming.description:
Streaming mode. Default: on for videos and music if the settings'
`streamMedia` is, by the link's extension, then by the file's real
name once the server answers.

userAgent.description: The browser's user agent, sent instead of Ottie's, the same way.

jobs.description: Added in this order, each as `POST /jobs` would.

token.description: Its token, shown this once: Ottie keeps only a hash of it.

ids.description:
One per job sent, in the same order: its new ID, or null if it was
refused.

refused.description: Why each refused one was, by its place in `jobs`.

AddedWithin.description:
How recently a download was added; "today" starts at local midnight
where the list is shown.

AllowedFolders.description:
Where devices may have downloads written, besides every category's
folder (and what's inside them). The computer running Ottie isn't limited.

error.description: English: for logs, and for codes a client doesn't know.

ApiError.description:
Body of every error answer: English text, plus a code (and details) for
clients to translate.

Appearance.description:
How the front ends look: light, dark or as the system says, and which
pair of themes.

Arrangement.description: How a list of downloads is laid out.

grouped.description: Grouped by status, each group sorted.

BuiltIn.description: The categories Ottie itself needs; they can't be removed.

ByteRange.description: A part of the file that one connection fetches.

Category.description:
A category: where its downloads go and which files it takes. As listed
by `GET /categories` and sent in `categoryChanged` events.

oneOf.description: Null for the user's own categories.

extensions.description: Lowercase, without the dot. Each belongs to one category at most.

folder.description: Where its downloads are saved; null: each download must name a folder.

maxConcurrent.description: How many of its downloads may run at once; 0 = no cap of its own.

speedLimit.description: Bytes per second for all its downloads together; 0 = none.

CategoryBody.description:
Body of `POST /categories` and `PUT /categories/{id}`: every setting (a
PUT replaces them all).

extensions.description: With or without the dot, any case: `.MKV` and `mkv` are the same.

folder.description: An absolute folder; null or left out: none.

Device.description: A device with a token of its own.

created.description: When it was added, in milliseconds since 1970.

lastUsed.description: When its token was last used (to the minute), in milliseconds since 1970.

readOnly.description: It may look but not change anything.

oneOf.description: A job was added or changed state, name or settings.
Bytes arrived; sent a few times per second per running job.

ranges.description:
Several connections: each one's range, with what has arrived so
far. Empty for one connection.

oneOf.description: A job was removed (`DELETE /jobs/{id}`): drop it.
A category was added or changed: insert-or-replace by `id`.

A category was removed; its jobs were moved to General first (and a
`changed` event was sent for each).
The settings changed (from any client): all of them, as now.
A saved view was added or changed: insert-or-replace by `id`.
A saved view was removed.

A time slot was added or changed, or started or stopped applying:
insert-or-replace by `id`.
A time slot was removed (by hand, with its category, or once over).
Events were missed (the client was too slow): fetch `GET /jobs` again.

Event.description:
A message on the `GET /events` WebSocket. Connect first, then fetch
`GET /jobs`, then apply events in order (insert-or-replace by `id`, or
drop on `removed`).

Existing.description:
What a download does when a file with its name is already in its folder
(docs/decisions/0049).

oneOf.description: A link that can be added.

exists.description: A file named `name` is already in the folder it would be saved in.

known.description: A download of this same link is already on the list.

matched.description: The category it would get without one chosen.

name.description: The file name the link suggests; the server may give another.

url.description:
As it would be added (normalized: `HTTPS://Example.com` is
`https://example.com/`).

oneOf.description:
One that can't: `refused` says why (`invalidUrl` or
`unsupportedScheme`).

FoundLink.description: Something in the text that looks like a link (`scheme://…`).

nonce.description: 32 to 128 hex digits, random, new for each check.

proof.description:
HMAC-SHA256 of `ottie identity v1`, a line break, then the nonce,
keyed with this computer's token, as hex.

Job.description: One download, as listed by `GET /jobs` and sent in `changed` events.

error.description: Why it failed, or the last failure while `retrying`, in English.

fileName.description: Known once the server has answered.

heldBy.description: While `scheduled`: the time slot that keeps it from running, if one does.

id.description: Like `2026.10.12-14.03.07-1`; sorting by it sorts by creation.

moving.description:
Its file is moving to another category's folder. Until it's done, it
can't be paused, resumed, cancelled, removed or moved again.

place.description:
Its place in the queue: among the waiting downloads of its priority,
lower places start first. Only the order means something.

oneOf.description: The same, as a code to translate (see `Problem`).

ranges.description:
Downloads over several connections: each connection's range, as last
saved (`progress` events bring them live). Empty for one connection.

retries.description: Failed attempts since bytes last arrived.

speedLimit.description: Bytes per second; 0 = no limit of its own.

startAt.description:
While `scheduled`: when it joins the queue, in milliseconds since
1970 (UTC).

stopAt.description: When it pauses if it hasn't finished by then, the same way.

streaming.description:
Streaming mode: over several connections, the file comes in order,
its last 1 MiB first, so it can play while downloading.

total.description: Size in bytes, if the server said.

url.description: The link, without a password it holds (FTP: `ftp://user@host/…`).

waitingForBandwidth.description:
Downloading, but the speed limits give it no bandwidth for now: other
downloads take it all (urgent ones first).

JobChange.description:
Body of `PATCH /jobs/{id}`: the job's own settings to change; a field
left out stays as it is.

oneOf.description:
What to do if a file with its name is already in its folder: for one
that stopped to ask (`fileExists`), choose, then resume it.

speedLimit.description: Bytes per second; 0 = no limit of its own.

startAt.description:
Wait until then, in milliseconds since 1970 (UTC): a queued, paused,
failed or retrying download becomes `scheduled`; a running one stops
first. `null`: no start time (a scheduled download joins the queue
now, as it does for a time already past).

stopAt.description: Pause then, wherever it is; `null`: no stop time. After the start time.

streaming.description: Streaming mode. Once set, the file type no longer decides it.

destDir.description:
The folder it would be saved in, if not its category's: then the
folder decides the category.

Matched.description:
Answer to `POST /categories/match`: the category a download of that link
would get. The server's real file name may still move it, unless the user
picks the category or a folder.

byFolder.description:
The folder decided: it's this category's folder, or (Other) the
folder of none.

extension.description: The extension the link suggests, if any.

Palette.description: A light theme and a dark one that go together.

links.description: In the order found, each once.

destDir.description:
The folder they would be saved in, if not their categories': then
the folder decides their category.

text.description:
Any text: one link per line, an email, a web page. A sequence in a
link (`[001-120]`, `[a-z]`, `{small,large}`) gives each link it holds.

oneOf.description: Connecting or reading failed; `detail` is English.
Too many redirects, or one to something other than http(s).
The server answered with a status we can't use (404, 503…).
No data for this many seconds.
The connection closed before the end of the file.
The file kept changing on the server.
Writing the file failed; `detail` is English.

A file named `name` is already in the folder, and the download asks
what to do: resume it after choosing `existing` (`PATCH /jobs/{id}`).

The FTP server refused a command with reply `status` (530: the user
name or password, 550: no such file or no access…); `detail` is what
it said.

Neither the system nor the person trusts the FTPS server's
certificate: posting `host` and `fingerprint` (SHA-256, lowercase
hex) to `POST /certificates` trusts it; then resume the download.
An `ftpes://` link to a server that doesn't offer TLS.

Problem.description:
Why a job failed or is retrying. Clients translate it by `code` and
fall back to the job's English `error` for codes they don't know.

oneOf.description: The token is missing or wrong (401).
This device's token is read-only (403).

Only the computer running Ottie, with its token file's token, may do
this: manage devices and the folders they may use (403).

This device may not have downloads written there: only in a
category's folder or one listed in Settings or config.toml (403).
A device's name has 1 to 60 characters.

A part of the path isn't what it should be (a number ID that isn't
a number); `error` says what's wrong.
The body isn't the JSON expected; `error` says what's wrong.
`destDir` must be an absolute path.
No folder given, and the category has none.
The job's state doesn't allow it (resuming a completed job…).
A download's stop time must come after its start time.
A slot without a date needs at least one day.
A slot must allow or stop downloads, or set a limit.
Not `HH:MM` (a time) or `YYYY-MM-DD` (a date).
The new order must list every slot once.
General and Other can't be removed.

A value must be from `min` to `max`; `setting` is its field name
(`maxConcurrent`, `globalLimit`, `speedLimit`, `startAt`…).
Its file is moving; try again once it's done.
The download can't resume, so moving it now would start it over.
The file couldn't move (disk full, no permission…); `detail` says why.
Not a server's name and a certificate's SHA-256 (64 hex digits).
Not a language tag like `en` or `pt-BR`.
A play link that doesn't exist or has expired.
Played past what arrived, but the download failed or was cancelled.
The download started over while being played (its file changed).

A browser's `cookie`, `referrer` or `userAgent` (the field's name)
that can't be sent as a header: a line break, or over 32 KiB.
A `requestId` that isn't 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`.
More links at once than the setting `maxBatch` allows.

Saving the change to the database failed (a full disk, a drive gone):
nothing changed. `error` has the database's text (docs/decisions/0059).
The daemon is shutting down.
A bug or an unexpected failure; `error` has the details.

RefusedJob.description:
A job of `POST /jobs/batch` that wasn't added, and why: the error
`POST /jobs` would have answered.

oneOf.description: One place earlier.
One place later.
Before all the others.
After all the others.
Just before this download. Only those of its priority move.

before.description: Just before this download. Only those of its priority move.

oneOf.description: Just after this download.

Reorder.description:
Where to move downloads in the queue, among the waiting downloads of
their priority: `"up"`, `"down"`, `"top"`, `"bottom"`, or next to a
download, `{ "before": id }` or `{ "after": id }` (where it was dropped).

ids.description: The downloads to move. Those that aren't queued, scheduled or paused stay as they are.
Every slot, once, in the new order.

Settings.description:
What applies to the whole daemon, as `GET /settings` answers it and
`settingsChanged` events send it.

oneOf.description:
The look shared by the devices that choose to follow it; null until
one shares its own.

existing.description:
What a download does when a file with its name is already in its
folder, unless the one adding it said (`existing` in `POST /jobs`).

firstRetryWaitMs.description:
Wait before the first retry, in milliseconds; each next one waits
twice as long, up to a minute.

globalLimit.description: Bytes per second for all downloads together; 0 = no limit.

language.description:
The language those devices show, as a tag like `en` or `pt-BR`; null:
each shows its own system's. A device without it keeps its own.

maxBatch.description:
The most links added at once (`POST /jobs/batch`) or looked at
(`POST /jobs/preview`).

maxConcurrent.description: How many downloads run at once; the others wait. At least 1.

maxRetries.description:
A download that keeps failing with errors that may go away (a dropped
connection, a busy server) fails after this many retries in a row.
0 = never retry.

retriesBeforeYield.description: Retries a download makes before letting a waiting one go first.

setupDone.description:
The first-start setup (starter categories) was done or skipped;
until then, front ends offer it.

oneOf.description:
The last step of that setup someone went past (done or skipped), so
it carries on after it, in whichever front end; null: from the start.

storageFailing.description:
While Ottie can't save to its database (disk full, a drive gone), the
last error, in English; null when saving works. Not a setting: no
change sets it, and `settingsChanged` tells when it changes.

streamMedia.description:
New video and music downloads start in streaming mode, unless the
one adding them says otherwise.

SettingsChange.description:
Body of `PATCH /settings`: only the fields given change, all at once.
A value out of its range (see `crates/api/src/settings.rs`) refuses the
whole change with `outOfRange`.

language.description: `null`: each device shows its own system's language.

oneOf.description: `null`: the setup starts from its first step.

SetupStep.description:
A step of the first-start setup (docs/decisions/0050), in the order they
come. A front end shows those it has: the desktop app's own come last.

Slot.description:
A time slot (docs/decisions/0040), as `GET /slots` lists it and
`slotChanged` events send it.

category.description: The category it applies to; null: the whole queue.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`: it happens once, on that day, and is removed once over.

days.description:
The days it happens on, every week (Monday first); empty when it
happens once.

oneOf.description: What it does to downloads; null: nothing.

enabled.description: Off: kept, but it never applies.

letFinish.description: With `stop`: running downloads finish; only new ones wait.

maxConcurrent.description: How many downloads may run at once while it lasts; null: the usual.

place.description:
Its place in the list: lower comes first, and wins where two apply
to the same thing. Only the order means something.

speedLimit.description:
Bytes per second for the queue (or the category) while it lasts;
0 = no limit; null: the usual limit.

stayPaused.description:
With `stop`: when it ends, the downloads it held are paused (to be
resumed by hand) instead of carrying on.

to.description: `HH:MM`; on the next day if it isn't after `from` (the same: a whole day).

SlotBody.description:
Body of `POST /slots` and `PUT /slots/{id}`: a slot as set by the user.
Give `days` (every week) or a `date` (once). It must allow or stop
downloads, or set a limit.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`; given, the slot happens once and `days` is ignored.

SlotDownloads.description: What a slot does to downloads.

slots.description:
In the order of the list: where two apply to the same thing, the
higher one wins.

timeZone.description:
The time zone slots follow (the daemon's computer's), like
`Europe/Paris`; null if the system doesn't name it.

SpeedHistory.description: The total download speed over the last hour.

samples.description:
All downloads' speed together in bytes per second, one sample per
second, oldest first; the last is the latest. At most 3600.

url.description:
A path on the daemon (`/api/v1/stream/<ticket>/<name>`) that serves
the file to anyone who has it, without the token, with `Range`
support. Valid for 12 hours after its last use.

TrustCertificate.description: Body of `POST /certificates`: what a `certificate` problem says.

TrustedCertificate.description:
An FTPS server's certificate trusted by hand (docs/decisions/0054), as
`GET /certificates` lists them.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the certificate, 64 lowercase hex digits.

host.description: The server's name as in links, lowercase.

View.description:
A saved view: a name, which downloads it shows and how they're laid out.
Listed by `GET /views` and sent in `viewChanged` events.

ViewBody.description:
Body of `POST /views` and `PUT /views/{id}`: everything about the view
(a PUT replaces it all).

ViewFilters.description: Which downloads a view shows: those that pass every filter.

nameContains.description: Part of the file name, in any case; empty: any name.

states.description:
Null: any state. An empty list shows nothing. `connecting` counts as
`downloading` (the daemon saves it so).

token.description: The token from `ottie token` (or `<config folder>/token`): this computer's, or a device's from `POST /access/devices` (`ottie device add`). The events WebSocket takes it as the protocol `ottie.token.<token>` instead.
